purpose: Final algorithm/k/approach selection ONLY. No production artifact is read or written; centroid selection and artifact re-export (incl. refitting fitted_scaler.pkl on 11 features) are separate tasks.

step1_min_cluster_size_floor.citation: Bradley, Bennett & Demiriz (2000), constrained K-Means — size constraints added to avoid local solutions with empty clusters or clusters having very few points.
step1_min_cluster_size_floor.approach_a_note: Approach A fits an independent model per age band, so the floor is applied within every band; the binding figure is the smallest cluster share in any band.

methodology.step2_macro_silhouette: Mean silhouette within each cluster first, then mean across clusters (unweighted by size) — less biased by imbalanced/outlier-driven splits than the micro average.
methodology.step3_ranking: Rank-sum over macro-silhouette (primary), Davies-Bouldin and Calinski-Harabasz, within each approach. CH is NOT comparable across approaches (scales with n); cross-approach comparison uses macro-silhouette and Davies-Bouldin only. Framework: Akhanli & Hennig (2020) Statistics and Computing 30:1523-1544.
methodology.step4a_density_validation: Mean AND proportion-meeting-benchmark per cluster, per Metzler, Zhou & Grace (2021)'s own proportion-based validation, plus Sarle's bimodality coefficient and a 1-vs-2-component GMM BIC check so a healthy mean cannot hide a split population.
methodology.step4b_single_axis_diagnostic: Per-cluster means across all 11 features; per-feature spread (max-min cluster mean) expressed in robust-scaled (IQR) units, the same geometry the clustering saw. Tests the Metzler et al. 'split on one trivial axis' pattern.

step5_conclusion: FALLBACK APPLIES. Across all 38 combinations passing the 5% size floor, the two halves of the usability gate never co-occur: every combination whose clusters order monotonically across the 5 external benchmarks discriminates on them by <=7pp (uninformative), and every combination that discriminates materially has clusters that are not ordered (multi-directional archetypes, not health tiers). This is the signature of users lying on a continuum with two largely independent axes (accumulation vs. protection) rather than in discrete health groups; a percentile-band score is the more defensible design than forcing hard clusters.
